question: Which metric or evaluation rule should be used for the next BraTS inpainting competition?
edition_scope: BraTS 2027 is the author's intended application, not a claim about announced 2027 rules. The external reference is the published 2026 task and evaluator.
assessment_scope: Documentary assessment of existing experiments, protocols and code. No new metric experiment, patient-data analysis or competition ranking was executed.
coverage_definition: Coverage describes what has actually been investigated. It is not a percentage of the overall problem solved, a quality score or a metric recommendation.

questions.question: What should a winning reconstruction preserve?
questions.evidence: The ladder separates reference distortion, residual amplitude, target alignment and acquisition. Synthetic controls distinguish omitted from incorrect detail. The task may value a particular observed healthy region, plausible counterfactual tissue or downstream utility; those are different targets.
questions.decision_progress: Specify the evaluation target before assigning a metric failure. A conditional mean can be optimal for squared-error prediction, so its advantage alone does not establish a bad competition ranking.
questions.missing: Organizer agreement on acceptable uncertainty and the relative costs of blur, plausible but incorrect anatomy and downstream failure. No patient-specific healthy counterfactual is observed inside an actual lesion.

questions.question: What does the implemented evaluator actually measure?
questions.evidence: Saved inpainting 0.0.12 probes with torchmetrics 1.1.2 and 1.9.0 inspect tensor-axis behavior, percentile normalization, PSNR clipping and within-case ordering. They are synthetic code probes, not official-server reproduction.
questions.decision_progress: Freeze implementation, shape convention, mask support, data range, clipping and versions. Metric names alone are insufficient to specify the competition rule.
questions.missing: A container pinned to the actual organizer deployment, server parity, exceptional-input handling and accepted 3D orientation/boundary behavior on challenge volumes.

questions.question: Does a metric notice removal of individual detail?
questions.evidence: Analytical and synthetic averaging/attenuation controls, a provisional QTIM mean-versus-mirror profile, and face pixel/identity-reference disagreements expose score interpretations. Different face measurement scopes are explicit.
questions.decision_progress: Require an attenuation/mean control and report how it changes the score. A high pixel or stranger-calibrated rank alone cannot establish correct individual detail.
questions.missing: Validated BraTS reconstructions showing loss of recoverable target-specific detail, separated from uncertainty, registration and acquisition. Evidence that an alternative metric improves actual model decisions.

questions.question: Does it distinguish wrong detail from missing detail?
questions.evidence: Norm-matched wrong residuals, attenuation and noise distinguish magnitude from target direction. QTIM T3a/T3b and T2 are separate tests; a failed superiority test is not equivalence. Constructed controls do not supply clinical error costs.
questions.decision_progress: Reject interpreting residual magnitude or visual realism alone as correct anatomy. State the desired tradeoff before evaluating a candidate distance.
questions.missing: Matched-realism anatomical errors in actual 3D model outputs, independent error labels and agreed penalties for hallucination versus omission.

questions.question: Can nuisance acquisition differences be separated from anatomical error?
questions.evidence: Repeat captures across modalities, synthetic pupil dilation and HACA3 stage-1 paired contrast shifts probe acquisition sensitivity. HACA3 contrast reduction is not a demonstration of preserved individual structure.
questions.decision_progress: Use repeat/acquisition controls separately from wrong-anatomy controls. Invariance is valuable only if it does not erase information relevant to the selected task.
questions.missing: Accepted MRI registration/QC, scanner/site/contrast stratification and a measurement of both nuisance tolerance and sensitivity to real anatomical errors.

questions.question: Does the score reflect anatomical structure and useful downstream behavior?
questions.evidence: Label robustness explores Dice and simple shape/topology descriptors under threshold segmentation and different priors. CARE is a released-score aggregation audit. Neither validates real BraTS downstream anatomy.
questions.decision_progress: Do not assume that adding Dice, a topology descriptor or a segmentation pipeline automatically fixes averaging bias. Specify structure, reference labels and downstream purpose.
questions.missing: Real 3D MRI with independently checked anatomical labels, blinded or task-relevant error assessments, and actual parcellation/registration/segmentation outcomes.

questions.question: Is the result stable across 3D masks, tissue regions and scales?
questions.coverage: Partial spatial coverage; challenge transfer untested
questions.evidence: Random brain windows, historical size/shell sweeps and Gaussian spatial maps localize variation. The latest object-relative sweep is specified but not established as completed. Cross-anatomy domains stress mechanisms rather than validate BraTS transfer.
questions.decision_progress: Report mask size, geometry, anatomical location and boundary separately instead of assuming a scalar average describes all voids.
questions.missing: Irregular challenge masks, 3D continuity, boundary seams, small critical structures and prespecified size/site strata in actual model outputs.

questions.question: Do candidate metrics make useful distinctions among real inpainting methods?
questions.coverage: Not tested in a valid comparative BraTS experiment
questions.evidence: Donor fills and artificial controls are available. Frozen protocols mention challenge models, but a protocol, cached model or fixed illustration is not a completed model-level comparison. Withdrawn real-case results are excluded.
questions.decision_progress: The present evidence can expose failure modes; it cannot identify the metric that best ranks a U-Net, diffusion model or other competition entry.
questions.missing: Frozen predictions from several genuinely different methods on shared held-out BraTS cases, with controls and endpoint-specific eligibility.

questions.question: What independent criterion establishes that one metric gives a better decision?
questions.coverage: Proxy references; no direct MRI criterion validation
questions.evidence: Known latent synthetic structure and the whole-image ArcFace donor reference constrain interpretation. Neither is an independent reference for local healthy-brain completion quality.
questions.decision_progress: Metric-to-metric agreement is not validity. Validate against an independently defined anatomy/error/usefulness criterion, keeping uncertainty in that criterion.
questions.missing: Blinded MRI reader assessment or independently adjudicated task errors on an untouched validation split, with agreement and uncertainty reported.

questions.question: Will the aggregation produce a stable, non-redundant leaderboard?
questions.coverage: Metric dependence/probes partial; model ranks untested
questions.evidence: Within-case monotonicity is known for several MSE-derived variants; actual plain PSNR clipping breaks exact rank identity in the saved probe. Rung correlations and family/position intervals exist, but are not bootstrap confidence for a competition-method ranking.
questions.decision_progress: Check effective weighting of correlated distances, per-case versus pooled aggregation, ties, missing runs and case-bootstrap rank stability before adopting a rank sum or composite.
questions.missing: Method-by-case scores and independent quality labels; rank/reversal uncertainty across cases and strata; frozen weights and a prespecified treatment of failed cases.

questions.question: How should stochastic outputs and unavoidable ambiguity be scored fairly?
questions.evidence: Averaging/shrinkage mechanisms motivate separating a point prediction from a distribution of plausible completions. Saved donor averages are not a model ensemble or a calibrated predictive distribution.
questions.decision_progress: Freeze whether the competition requests one output or several, the sampling budget and selection rule. Do not mix best-of-N, mean-of-N and one-sample evaluations without specifying their different targets.
questions.missing: Repeated predictions from stochastic methods, fixed sample/compute budgets and validation of an appropriate quality/diversity or probabilistic evaluation rule.

questions.question: Can the chosen rule run reliably and reproducibly in the competition?
questions.coverage: Partial engineering evidence; no deployment validation
questions.evidence: Versioned aggregate artifacts, validity-mask tests, source hashes, a metric registry and the existing repository test run support reproducibility practice. Advanced endpoints remain blocked or absent; the historical Python-version guard failure is retained.
questions.decision_progress: Treat deterministic preprocessing, failures, runtime, dependencies and reference availability as selection criteria, separate from scientific validity.
questions.missing: Pinned evaluator container, measured runtime/memory at challenge scale, deterministic reference behavior, licensing/access checks and a hidden-test deployment rehearsal.
